text:
sophia: Quick question about client config for VPC/private endpoints + proxies. I'm seeing two odd things when using the Node SDK behind our corporate proxy + a custom base URL: 1) Host header seems to get set to the proxy host instead of the private endpoint, which breaks routing; 2) long-lived streaming requests (server-sent chunks) drop after ~60s with a TLS close. Anyone seen this and have recommended client config patterns?

ben: Yep saw both. For host header issue you need to explicitly set the Host header to the private host (if your proxy rewrites it). Also ensure you use tunnel mode (HTTP CONNECT) for TLS through the proxy so SNI/Host is preserved.

olivia: For Node specifically, we do something like:```js
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTP_PROXY, { keepAlive: true });
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseURL: process.env.REDWOOD_PRIVATE_URL, // e.g. https://private.redwood.internal
  headers: { Host: 'private.redwood.internal' },
  httpsAgent: agent
});
```
That preserves Host and keeps the socket alive.

harry: On the streaming side, corporate proxies sometimes kill idle streams. Two mitigations: 1) enable smaller keepalive pings from client if supported, 2) use chunk heartbeat (send a small comment/keepalive token) from server side. If you can't change server, reconnect logic with resume is necessary.

sophia: Are there recommended retry/backoff semantics for streams? I want to avoid hammering the private endpoint when network flaps.

ben: Exponential backoff with jitter is the usual. For streaming reconnects we use: initial 500ms, *2 up to 8s, jitter +/-25%, and cap total attempts to 6. Also add a short random delay before re-registering to avoid thundering herd.

olivia: Another gotcha: mTLS. If your private endpoint requires client certs, the proxy may need delegation or you must tunnel. In Go we use a custom transport:```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{Certificates: []tls.Certificate{clientCert}, InsecureSkipVerify: false},
  Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment,
  DisableKeepAlives: false,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0} // streaming
```
If you set Timeout != 0 it can cancel long streams.

harry: Also check the proxy's response buffering. Some proxies buffer entire response before releasing; that will break streaming semantics. If you control the proxy, enable streaming passthrough.

devex-bot: FYI doc: https://internal.docs/redwood/devex/proxy-vpc-streaming (linked) :bookmark_tabs:

sophia: thanks — last thing: environment variables vs explicit baseURL in SDK. Which wins?

ben: SDK reads explicit config first, then env. If you pass baseURL in constructor it overrides REDWOOD_BASE_URL. We recommend constructor for app code and env for CI/ops.

olivia: If you need per-route overrides, set route-level baseURL or use a custom request middleware to rewrite host for specific paths.

harry: If anyone wants, I can drop a small gist with a Node reconnect example that preserves stream position using our resume token header.

sophia: please do, that would help. I'll try the Host header + tunnel approach and report back. :thumbsup:
